question:
During triage in Modern SQL Mastery Advanced Queries, an engineer observes:
"System fault during operation: Running Total Generates Identical Duplicate Numbers on Duplicate Dates".
What is the verified root cause?

options.text: Window frame specification uses default RANGE frame instead of ROWS frame, causing rows with identical ORDER BY keys to sum together simultaneously.
The running total resets to zero every time the sale_date changes, so each new date starts counting from scratch instead of continuing the cumulative sum.
The rows are not sorted by sale_date before the cumulative sum is computed, so amounts are added in an arbitrary order that happens to repeat values when dates collide.
The accumulator variable is reinitialized inside the loop instead of before it, so every row after the first duplicate date reads a stale value from the previous iteration only.

explanation:
Root Cause: Window frame specification uses default RANGE frame instead of ROWS frame, causing rows with identical ORDER BY keys to sum together simultaneously.

Fix Resolution:
Change window frame to: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW.
